name: SW-200D tilt switch (Grove)
description: Tilt detector: an SW-200D two-ball, single-direction tilt switch wired between VCC and SIG, with a 10 kOhm pull-down from SIG to GND. The switch closes when the gold-pin end points down by more than about 10 degrees (the board standing upright), so SIG reads HIGH; tipping it more than about 10 degrees toward the silver-pin end opens it and SIG reads LOW. It only reports on/off, not the angle. Runs on 3-5.25 V. Sold as: Seeed Studio Grove - Tilt Switch (SW-200D) (Grove connector SIG, NC, VCC, GND; SW-200D between VCC and SIG with a 10 kOhm pull-down).
eli5: Two tiny metal balls roll inside a can: when the board stands up they touch the contacts and your board reads 1, when you tip it over they roll away and it reads 0.

pins.name: SIG
pins.description: Signal (Grove pin 1, yellow wire): HIGH (= VCC) while the switch is closed, LOW while open (10 kOhm pull-down on the board).

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply 3-5.25 V (Grove pin 3, red wire). Use 3V3 with an ESP32 or Pico, because SIG is switched to this voltage.

buildNotes: Grove connector order: SIG (yellow), NC (white), VCC (red), GND (black). Use a Grove-to-female-jumper cable to reach the breadboard.
On an ESP32 or Pico connect VCC to 3V3: the closed switch puts VCC straight onto SIG, so 5 V on VCC puts 5 V on the GPIO.
SIG is active HIGH for 'switch closed': 1 while the gold-pin end of the SW-200D points down (board upright), 0 when tipped more than about 10 degrees toward the silver-pin end.
The board already has a 10 kOhm pull-down on SIG; do not enable an internal pull-up.
The balls bounce for about 2 ms at each change; the driver waits 20 ms for a stable level.

example.code:
from sw200d import SW200D
import time

sw = SW200D({SIG})
while True:
    print('Tilt switch: %s' % ('CLOSED' if sw.is_closed() else 'open'))
    time.sleep(0.5)

test.title: Reports the switch closing when the board is set upright
